Explore the vsim repo at /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim (read-only). Goal: gather what is needed to plan an "L2C MMIO register replay" feature in the hybrid resume path (restore L2 cache controller config registers at 0xE0500000 via Debug Module Program Buffer stores before dret).

Report on:
1. src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp — the exact Program Buffer machinery: how progbuf is written, how abstract commands execute it, how cmderr is checked/cleared, the existing pb_* helpers (pb_v_data_sweep, the vsetvl Tier B path, set_gpr_block_load/set_fpr_block_load), and the exact ordering of steps inside resume() (mstatus.VS, V sweep, CSR restores, GPR loop, dcsr.prv, dret). Where would a "PB store to MMIO addresses" step naturally slot in, and which scratch GPRs are safe to use at that point? Is there an existing helper that stages a 64-bit immediate into a GPR via abstract command then executes PB code?
2. src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp — drain ordering, and whether there is any existing mechanism to READ memory/MMIO from the halted hart (PB loads?) that a drain-side L2C register read-back could reuse.
3. How capability gating works in the hybrid layer: how the code decides a CSR/feature exists on this engine (mmsc_cfg probing? config flags passed in? engine describe?). Look for how HYBRID_FLAG_* gate restore blocks, and whether there's any runtime probe of mmsc_cfg bit 46 (L2C present).
4. tests/hybrid/ — the recording_bus.hpp duck-typed DMI test double and 1-2 representative unit tests for a PB-based restore (e.g. V data sweep test or the vsetvl Tier B test): file names, test names, assertion style, so a new L2C-replay unit test can copy the pattern.
5. Engine configs: for each build/V*/obj_sc/config.inc present, report NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB (and core name). Also check the source config system (config.yaml, cmake, data/) for how NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB would be turned on to build an L2C-enabled engine variant, and whether any existing engine already has L2C>0.
6. Where hart PB load/store bus traffic gets decoded: does a PB store to 0xE0500000 (NDS_L2C_REG_BASE) reach the cluster-internal L2C register block, or does it route to the SystemC platform (src/platform/memory_map.h has no L2C entry)? Check the cpu cluster wrapper (e.g. src/cpu_wrappers/ax45mpv_premium_cpu_cluster_subsystem.hpp, has_shared_cache) and simulator.hpp bus decode / what happens on an access to an address outside memory_map.h ranges.
7. Whether HYBRID_* wire-format headers are consumed from external/andesim_abi — confirm the ABI submodule path and how version checks (hybrid_state_v1 version field) are enforced in this repo.

Return: concrete file paths + line-level facts (short quotes where load-bearing), the resume() step ordering as a numbered list, the answer to each question, and any constraint that would block PB stores to L2C registers. No file dumps.

35	// "Execute Program Buffer only" command (Debug Spec table 3.1):
36	//   cmdtype  = 0 (Access Register)
37	//   aarsize  = Bits64 (3) - ignored by DM when transfer=0, set for consistency
38	//   postexec = 1 (bit 18)
39	//   transfer = 0 (bit 17 NOT set) - skip register I/O, only run progbuf
40	//   write    = 0 (irrelevant when transfer=0)
41	//   regno    = 0 (irrelevant when transfer=0)
42	inline constexpr uint32_t kExecProgbufCmd =
43	    (uint32_t(AarSize::Bits64) & 0x7u) << 20 | (1u << 18);
44	
45	// Encode `vsetvl rd, rs1, rs2` (RVV 1.0 section 6.2, funct7=1000000).
46	// Tier-B restore: stage vl in rs1 and vtype in rs2 via Abstract Commands,
47	// then branch-free-restore both in one Program Buffer execution.
48	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_vsetvl(uint8_t rd, uint8_t rs1, uint8_t rs2)
49	{
50	    return (0b1000000u << 25)
51	         | ((uint32_t(rs2) & 0x1Fu) << 20)
52	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
53	         | (0b111u << 12)
54	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
55	         | 0x57u;  // OP-V opcode
56	}
57	
58	// Encode `csrrw rd, csr, rs1` (SYSTEM opcode, funct3=001).
59	// Tier-A PB fallback: stage the CSR value in rs1 via Abstract Command,
60	// then write it to a CSR that the DM cannot reach via abstract access.
61	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_csrrw(uint8_t rd, uint16_t csr, uint8_t rs1)
62	{
63	    return ((uint32_t(csr) & 0xFFFu) << 20)
64	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
65	         | (0b001u << 12)
66	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
67	         | 0x73u;  // SYSTEM opcode
68	}
69	
70	// Encode `csrrs rd, csr, rs1` (SYSTEM opcode, funct3=010). With rs1=x0 this is
71	// `csrr rd, csr`: a pure CSR read (the RISC-V spec suppresses the write side
72	// effect when rs1=x0). The CSR drain sweep reads each supported Andes/M-ext CSR
73	// into a temp GPR with this, then sd's it to the scratch page.
74	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_csrrs(uint8_t rd, uint16_t csr, uint8_t rs1)
75	{
76	    return ((uint32_t(csr) & 0xFFFu) << 20)
77	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
78	         | (0b010u << 12)
79	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
80	         | 0x73u;  // SYSTEM opcode
81	}
82	
83	// Encode `vle8.v vd, (rs1)` - unit-stride vector load, EEW=8 (RVV 1.0 sec 7.4).
84	// Fields: vm=1 (unmasked, bit 25), width=000, mop=00, mew=0, nf=000,
85	// lumop=00000, opcode LOAD-FP=0x07. PB V-regfile reload sweeps v0..v31 from
86	// the shared scratch region after a vsetvl to e8/m1.
87	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_vle8_v(uint8_t vd, uint8_t rs1)
88	{
89	    return (1u << 25)
90	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
91	         | ((uint32_t(vd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
92	         | 0x07u;  // LOAD-FP opcode
93	}
94	
95	// Encode `vse8.v vs3, (rs1)` - unit-stride vector store, EEW=8. Mirror of
96	// encode_vle8_v with opcode STORE-FP=0x27. PB V-regfile dump sweeps v0..v31
97	// back to the shared scratch region at drain.
98	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_vse8_v(uint8_t vs3, uint8_t rs1)
99	{
100	    return (1u << 25)
101	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
102	         | ((uint32_t(vs3) & 0x1Fu) << 7)
103	         | 0x27u;  // STORE-FP opcode
104	}
105	
106	// Encode `addi rd, rs1, imm12` (OP-IMM opcode 0x13, funct3=000). The batched
107	// V-data sweep advances the scratch base pointer x7 by one register-span
108	// between transfers WITHIN a Program-Buffer execution, so the per-register
109	// abstract x7 write disappears. imm12 is a signed 12-bit field (-2048..2047).
110	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_addi(uint8_t rd, uint8_t rs1, int32_t imm12)
111	{
112	    return ((uint32_t(imm12) & 0xFFFu) << 20)
113	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
114	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
115	         | 0x13u;  // OP-IMM opcode (funct3=000)
116	}
117	
118	// Encode `ld rd, imm12(rs1)` (LOAD opcode 0x03, funct3=011 for 64-bit). The GPR
119	// block-load sweeps x1..x31 from a scratch region addressed by a base register,
120	// so 31 abstract register writes collapse into a few Program-Buffer executions.
121	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_ld(uint8_t rd, uint8_t rs1, int32_t imm12)
122	{
123	    return ((uint32_t(imm12) & 0xFFFu) << 20)
124	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
125	         | (0b011u << 12)
126	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
127	         | 0x03u;  // LOAD opcode
128	}
129	
130	// Encode `fld rd, imm12(rs1)` (LOAD-FP opcode 0x07, funct3=011 for double). Same
131	// shape as encode_ld with the FP-load opcode: the FPR block-load sweeps f0..f31
132	// from the scratch region via an integer base register, collapsing 32 abstract
133	// FPR writes into a few Program-Buffer executions.
134	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_fld(uint8_t rd, uint8_t rs1, int32_t imm12)
135	{
136	    return ((uint32_t(imm12) & 0xFFFu) << 20)
137	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
138	         | (0b011u << 12)
139	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
140	         | 0x07u;  // LOAD-FP opcode
141	}
142	
143	// Encode `sd rs2, imm12(rs1)` (STORE opcode 0x23, funct3=011 for 64-bit). The
144	// mirror of encode_ld for the DRAIN direction: the GPR drain sweeps x1..x30 from
145	// the regfile INTO the scratch region via an integer base register, collapsing
146	// 31 abstract reads into a few Program-Buffer executions. S-type splits the
147	// signed 12-bit immediate: imm[11:5] -> bits 31:25, imm[4:0] -> bits 11:7.
148	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_sd(uint8_t rs2, uint8_t rs1, int32_t imm12)
149	{
150	    const uint32_t imm = uint32_t(imm12) & 0xFFFu;
151	    return ((imm >> 5) & 0x7Fu) << 25
152	         | ((uint32_t(rs2) & 0x1Fu) << 20)
153	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
154	         | (0b011u << 12)
155	         | ((imm & 0x1Fu) << 7)
156	         | 0x23u;  // STORE opcode
157	}
158	
159	// Encode `fsd rs2, imm12(rs1)` (STORE-FP opcode 0x27, funct3=011 for double).
160	// Same S-type shape as encode_sd with the FP-store opcode: the FPR drain sweeps
161	// f0..f31 from the regfile into the scratch region via an integer base register.
162	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_fsd(uint8_t rs2, uint8_t rs1, int32_t imm12)
163	{
164	    const uint32_t imm = uint32_t(imm12) & 0xFFFu;
165	    return ((imm >> 5) & 0x7Fu) << 25
166	         | ((uint32_t(rs2) & 0x1Fu) << 20)
167	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
168	         | (0b011u << 12)
169	         | ((imm & 0x1Fu) << 7)
170	         | 0x27u;  // STORE-FP opcode
171	}
172	
173	// Write insns[0..n-1] to progbuf0..n-1 and kEbreak to progbuf[n].
174	// Clears any sticky abstractcs.cmderr (W1C), issues kExecProgbufCmd, polls
175	// until abstractcs.busy clears, then verifies cmderr stayed clear.
176	//
177	// Throws std::runtime_error if insns.size() > kProgbufMaxInsns, if the poll
178	// times out, or if the DM raises cmderr during execution. No caller has a
179	// legitimate reason to silently continue on PB failure - the hart state
180	// would be partially restored / partially drained, which is worse than
181	// surfacing the fault.
182	template<typename Bus>
183	inline void exec_progbuf(Bus& bus, std::span<const uint32_t> insns)
184	{
185	    if (insns.size() > kProgbufMaxInsns)
186	        throw std::runtime_error(
187	            "exec_progbuf: too many instructions ("
188	            + std::to_string(insns.size()) + " > "
189	            + std::to_string(kProgbufMaxInsns) + ")");
190	
191	    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < insns.size(); ++i)
192	        bus.write(static_cast<uint8_t>(kProgbuf0 + i), insns[i]);
193	    bus.write(static_cast<uint8_t>(kProgbuf0 + insns.size()), kEbreak);
194	
195	    if ((bus.read(kDmiAbstractcs) & kAbstractcsCmderrMask) != 0u)
196	        bus.write(kDmiAbstractcs, kAbstractcsCmderrMask);
197	
198	    bus.write(kDmiCommand, kExecProgbufCmd);
199	    poll_until_clear(bus, kDmiAbstractcs, kAbstractcsBusy, "exec_progbuf busy");
200	
201	    const uint32_t cmderr = bus.read(kDmiAbstractcs) & kAbstractcsCmderrMask;
202	    if (cmderr != 0u)
203	        throw std::runtime_error(
204	            "exec_progbuf: PB execution raised cmderr="
205	            + std::to_string(cmderr >> 8));
206	}
207	
208	// vtype encoding for e8, m8, ta, ma (vsew=000, vlmul=011, vta=1, vma=1). The
209	// V-data sweep uses LMUL=8 so one vle8.v/vse8.v moves a whole group of 8
210	// registers (8*vlenb byte-elements, vl=8*vlenb) in a single instruction.
211	inline constexpr uint32_t kVtypeE8M8 = 0xC3u;
212	
213	// Abstract-command write of a 64-bit value to Debug Module register `regno`
214	// (GPR/CSR/FPR): DATA0/DATA1 + Access-Register(write) + busy-poll. Free
215	// function so ResumeDriver, StateDrain, and the V-data sweep share one copy.
216	template<typename Bus>
217	inline void write_register_abstract(Bus& bus, uint16_t regno, uint64_t value)
218	{
219	    bus.write(kDmiData0, static_cast<uint32_t>(value & 0xffffffffu));
220	    bus.write(kDmiData1, static_cast<uint32_t>((value >> 32) & 0xffffffffu));
221	    bus.write(kDmiCommand,
222	              access_register_command(regno, AarSize::Bits64, /*write=*/true));
223	    poll_until_clear(bus, kDmiAbstractcs, kAbstractcsBusy,
224	                     "write_register_abstract");
225	}
226	
227	// Program-Buffer block sweep: seed integer base register `base_gpr` with
228	// `base_gpa`, then run `encode(reg, base_gpr, (reg-first_reg)*8)` for reg in
229	// [first_reg, last_reg) through the Program Buffer, batched at (progbufsize-1)
230	// instructions per execution (one slot reserved for the terminating ebreak).
231	// One uniform load/store encoder drives it, so the GPR/FPR restore (ld/fld,
232	// scratch -> regfile) and the GPR/FPR drain (sd/fsd, regfile -> scratch) share
233	// one implementation: ~32 registers move in ~6 halted-hart round-trips instead
234	// of ~32 abstract commands, and the values ride the shared scratch page, not
235	// DMI. The 8-byte-strided offset spans every slot (<= 248, within ld/sd's
236	// signed 12-bit immediate). The caller guarantees base_gpr is safe to seed: on
237	// a load it may be a swept register that rides LAST (its own load runs after
238	// every other use of it as the base); on a store it must be EXCLUDED from
239	// [first_reg, last_reg) -- seeding destroys its value before it could be stored
240	// -- and captured separately.
241	template<typename Bus>
242	inline void pb_block_sweep(Bus& bus, uint8_t base_gpr, uint64_t base_gpa,
243	                           uint8_t first_reg, uint8_t last_reg,
244	                           uint32_t (*encode)(uint8_t, uint8_t, int32_t))
245	{
246	    // The Program Buffer holds abstractcs.progbufsize entries (this DM reports
247	    // 8); reserve one slot for the terminating ebreak, so at most progbufsize-1
248	    // load/store insns per execution.
249	    const uint32_t progbufsize = (bus.read(kDmiAbstractcs) >> 24) & 0x1Fu;
250	    const std::size_t max_ops = (progbufsize > 1) ? progbufsize - 1u : 1u;
251	    write_register_abstract(bus, regno_gpr(base_gpr), base_gpa);  // base pointer
252	    std::array<uint32_t, 32> batch{};
253	    std::size_t n = 0;
254	    for (uint8_t k = first_reg; k < last_reg; ++k) {
255	        batch[n++] = encode(k, base_gpr,
256	                            static_cast<int32_t>((k - first_reg) * 8));
257	        if (n == max_ops || k + 1 == last_reg) {
258	            exec_progbuf(bus, std::span<const uint32_t>{batch.data(), n});
259	            n = 0;
260	        }
261	    }
262	}
263	
264	// Direction for csr_sweep: Restore writes each CSR from the scratch page
265	// (ld + csrrw), Drain reads each CSR back to scratch (csrr + sd).
266	enum class CsrSweepDir { Restore, Drain };
267	
268	// Program-Buffer CSR sweep: transport a caps-supported list of CSRs between the
269	// hart and the scratch page. Unlike pb_block_sweep (one uniform ld/st per
270	// register), a CSR needs TWO instructions -- the CSR number is baked into the
271	// csrrw/csrr immediate, so it cannot be a runtime operand -- so this batches at
272	// (progbufsize-1)/2 CSRs per Program-Buffer execution:
273	//   Restore: ld val,(k*8)(base); csrrw x0, csrs[k], val   (scratch -> CSR)
274	//   Drain:   csrr val, csrs[k];  sd val,(k*8)(base)       (CSR -> scratch)
275	// `base` is an integer GPR seeded once with `base_gpa` (the CSR scratch region);
276	// `val` is a temp GPR the caller may clobber. The values ride the shared scratch
277	// page (staged/lifted by stage_csr_to_scratch / read_csr_from_scratch), not DMI.
278	// The csrs list is the caps-supported set in the SAME canonical order the host
279	// stager packs, so slot k*8 holds csrs[k]'s value. Empty list -> no-op (not even
280	// the base seed). The k*8 offset spans every slot (<= 81*8 = 648 < 2047).
281	//
282	// Every csrs[k] MUST be implemented by the target (the caller builds the list
283	// from caps): a csrrw/csrr to an unimplemented CSR raises cmderr and exec_progbuf
284	// throws, aborting the whole batch. That is intentional -- a faulting sweep means
285	// the caps map is wrong, a config bug to fix, not something to silently mirror.
286	// To make that bug FIXABLE, a faulting batch is re-run one CSR at a time and the
287	// thrown error names the offending CSR (re-running is safe: drain reads are
288	// idempotent, and a restore re-applies the same staged values).
289	template<typename Bus>
290	inline void csr_sweep(Bus& bus, uint8_t base_gpr, uint64_t base_gpa,
291	                      uint8_t val_gpr, std::span<const uint16_t> csrs,
292	                      CsrSweepDir dir)
293	{
294	    if (csrs.empty()) return;
295	    const uint32_t progbufsize = (bus.read(kDmiAbstractcs) >> 24) & 0x1Fu;
296	    // Two insns per CSR; reserve one slot for the terminating ebreak. Clamp to
297	    // the ebreak-adjusted payload cap so a batch never overruns the buffer.
298	    std::size_t usable = (progbufsize > 1) ? progbufsize - 1u : 1u;
299	    if (usable > kProgbufMaxInsns) usable = kProgbufMaxInsns;
300	    const std::size_t max_csrs = (usable >= 2) ? usable / 2u : 1u;
301	    write_register_abstract(bus, regno_gpr(base_gpr), base_gpa);  // scratch base
302	    // The (transport; ld/sd) insn pair for csrs[k], shared by the batch build
303	    // and the fault bisect so both run the identical instructions.
304	    const auto pair_for = [&](std::size_t k) -> std::array<uint32_t, 2> {
305	        const int32_t off = static_cast<int32_t>(k * 8);
306	        if (dir == CsrSweepDir::Restore)
307	            return {encode_ld(val_gpr, base_gpr, off),
308	                    encode_csrrw(0, csrs[k], val_gpr)};
309	        return {encode_csrrs(val_gpr, csrs[k], 0),
310	                encode_sd(val_gpr, base_gpr, off)};
311	    };
312	    std::array<uint32_t, 32> batch{};
313	    std::size_t n = 0, in_batch = 0;
314	    for (std::size_t k = 0; k < csrs.size(); ++k) {
315	        const auto pair = pair_for(k);
316	        batch[n++] = pair[0];
317	        batch[n++] = pair[1];
318	        if (++in_batch == max_csrs || k + 1 == csrs.size()) {
319	            try {
320	                exec_progbuf(bus, std::span<const uint32_t>{batch.data(), n});
321	            } catch (const std::runtime_error&) {
322	                for (std::size_t j = k + 1 - in_batch; j <= k; ++j) {
323	                    const auto one = pair_for(j);
324	                    try {
325	                        exec_progbuf(bus, std::span<const uint32_t>{one});
326	                    } catch (const std::runtime_error&) {
327	                        char addr[8];
328	                        std::snprintf(addr, sizeof addr, "0x%x", csrs[j]);
329	                        throw std::runtime_error(
330	                            std::string{"csr_sweep: CSR "} + addr
331	                            + " raised cmderr -- the caps map over-claims a CSR"
332	                              " the hart does not implement (fix andes_caps)");
333	                    }
334	                }
335	                throw;  // no single CSR reproduced the batch fault
336	            }
337	            n = 0;
338	            in_batch = 0;
339	        }
340	    }
341	}
342	
343	// Sweep all 32 V data registers between the hart regfile and the vlenb-packed
344	// scratch region via the Program Buffer. load=true issues vle8.v
345	// (scratch -> regfile, on resume); load=false issues vse8.v (regfile ->
346	// scratch, at drain). The leading vsetvl to e8/m8 sets vl=8*vlenb and forces
347	// vstart=0, so one unit-stride access covers a whole LMUL=8 group of 8
348	// registers. Uses x5/x6 (vsetvl operands) and x7 (group base pointer) as
349	// scratch. `vlenb` is the runtime per-register width; the scratch must be
350	// packed at vlenb stride (stage_v_to_scratch) so each 8-register group is
351	// contiguous.
352	template<typename Bus>
353	inline void pb_v_data_sweep(Bus& bus, uint64_t scratch_gpa, uint64_t vlenb,
354	                            bool load)
355	{
356	    // The scratch holds v0..v31 packed contiguously at vlenb stride (see
357	    // stage_v_to_scratch), so 8 consecutive registers form one LMUL=8 group.
358	    // One vle8.v/vse8.v then moves a whole group (8*vlenb contiguous bytes,
359	    // vl=8*vlenb) and all 32 registers transfer in 4 grouped ops -- whose 4
360	    // (transfer; addi) pairs fit in a SINGLE Program-Buffer execution. Each PB
361	    // execution is one halted-hart DM round-trip (~1000 sim cycles in the
362	    // busy-poll), so this is the floor: one vsetvl + one grouped execution. The
363	    // register bytes never cross DMI; they ride the shared mmap.
364	    constexpr unsigned     kRegsPerGroup   = 8;  // LMUL=8
365	    // kVtypeE8M8's vlmul field (bits 2:0) must encode this LMUL, so one grouped
366	    // vle8.v/vse8.v really covers kRegsPerGroup registers (integer LMUL=1<<vlmul;
367	    // 0xC3 & 7 == 3 -> LMUL 8).
368	    static_assert((1u << (kVtypeE8M8 & 0x7u)) == kRegsPerGroup,
369	                  "kVtypeE8M8 must encode LMUL = kRegsPerGroup");
370	    constexpr std::size_t  kGroupSweepInsns = (32 / kRegsPerGroup) * 2;  // (ld;addi)*4
371	    static_assert(kGroupSweepInsns <= kProgbufMaxInsns,
372	                  "the grouped sweep must fit one Program Buffer execution");
373	    const uint64_t group_bytes = static_cast<uint64_t>(kRegsPerGroup) * vlenb;
374	    if (group_bytes > 2047)  // addi imm12 is signed 12-bit; max 8*128 = 1024
375	        throw std::runtime_error(
376	            "pb_v_data_sweep: 8*vlenb exceeds the addi imm12 range");
377	
378	    // vsetvl to e8/m8 with AVL = 8*vlenb sets vl = VLMAX = 8*vlenb (one
379	    // byte-element per lane across the whole group) and forces vstart = 0.
380	    write_register_abstract(bus, regno_gpr(5), group_bytes);  // AVL
381	    write_register_abstract(bus, regno_gpr(6), kVtypeE8M8);   // e8, m8, ta, ma
382	    const std::array<uint32_t, 1> pb_vsetvl = { encode_vsetvl(0, 5, 6) };
383	    exec_progbuf(bus, std::span<const uint32_t>{pb_vsetvl});
384	
385	    // Base pointer x7 staged once; the in-buffer addi advances it one group at
386	    // a time. The group base register must be LMUL-aligned: v0/v8/v16/v24.
387	    write_register_abstract(bus, regno_gpr(7), scratch_gpa);
388	    const uint32_t addi_step =
389	        encode_addi(7, 7, static_cast<int32_t>(group_bytes));
390	    std::array<uint32_t, kGroupSweepInsns> group_sweep{};
391	    std::size_t n = 0;
392	    for (uint8_t g = 0; g < 32; g += kRegsPerGroup) {
393	        group_sweep[n++] = load ? encode_vle8_v(g, 7) : encode_vse8_v(g, 7);
394	        group_sweep[n++] = addi_step;  // last group's addi is harmless dead work
395	    }
396	    exec_progbuf(bus, std::span<const uint32_t>{group_sweep.data(), n});
397	}
398	
399	}  // namespace hybrid

1	// Andes-CSR capability gating.
2	//
3	// A core implements an Andes custom CSR only when the matching feature is
4	// configured into it (config.inc). Restoring a CSR the target core lacks can
5	// hang the DMI handshake -- observed on ax45mpv_premium for ucode (no DSP) and
6	// mecc_code (no ECC). So the resume/drain loops transport only the CSRs the
7	// target core supports, decided here from the core's feature gates.
8	//
9	// This header is Verilator/SystemC-free: it maps a CSR address to its gate and
10	// answers "does a core with these gates support this CSR". The binding of each
11	// gate to the core's compiled-in `_NDS_*` config macros lives in the sim binary
12	// (see andes_caps_from_config), so this stays unit-testable in isolation.
13	#ifndef ANDES_HYBRID_ANDES_CAPS_HPP
14	#define ANDES_HYBRID_ANDES_CAPS_HPP
15	
16	#include <cstdint>
17	#include <string>
18	#include <vector>
19	
20	#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
21	
22	namespace hybrid {
23	
24	// The hardware feature that gates each transported CSR. ALWAYS = unconditionally
25	// present (a base machine CSR every core has; never gated off). The first block
26	// gates the v3 Andes custom CSRs; the second block (UMODE..TRIGGER) gates the v4
27	// M-ext CSRs (HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST) -- standard + Andes M-mode CSRs whose
28	// existence depends on a privilege level or extension the core may not have.
29	enum class AndesGate : uint8_t {
30	  ALWAYS = 0,
31	  DSP,
32	  CODENSE,
33	  ZCMT,        // standard Zcmt table jump (jvt); NOT implied by CoDense
34	  POWERBRAKE,
35	  STACKSAFE,
36	  ECC,
37	  PMA,
38	  ILM,
39	  DLM,
40	  PERF_MONITOR,
41	  // The Andes PMNDS counter scheme (SPA: mmsc_cfg.PMNDS). RTL ground truth
42	  // (kv_csr_dec.v existent_csr): these CSRs exist iff PERFORMANCE_MONITOR
43	  // AND NOT SSCOFPMF -- a core with the standard Sscofpmf count-overflow
44	  // extension REPLACES the Andes scheme. The _UMODE/_SMODE variants add the
45	  // privilege term the spec conditions carry (PMNDS & misa[20] / misa[18]).
46	  PMNDS,        // Andes-scheme perf counters (perf monitor && !Sscofpmf)
47	  PMNDS_UMODE,  // PMNDS && U-mode
48	  PMNDS_SMODE,  // PMNDS && S-mode
49	  ALT_FP,       // umisc_ctl: spec ALT_FP_FMT|CST_CTL, RTL BF16_ARITH|ACE
50	  // v4 M-ext gates.
51	  UMODE,       // needs U-mode  (NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS >= 2)
52	  SMODE,       // needs S-mode  (NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS == 3)
53	  EPMP,        // ePMP / Smepmp (mseccfg)
54	  SMRNMI,      // resumable NMI (mnscratch/mnepc/mncause/mnstatus/mnvec/mrnxvec)
55	  EXCSLVL,     // exception save levels (msave*)
56	  CLIC,        // CLIC / enhanced CLIC (mtvt/mintthresh/mcirq_entry)
57	  SMSTATEEN,   // state-enable (mstateen0..3)
58	  CCTL,        // cache control CSRs (mcctlbeginaddr/mcctldata)
59	  PPI,         // private peripheral interface base (mppib)
60	  FIO,         // fast IO base (mfiob)
61	  TRIGGER,     // debug triggers (tselect/tdata1/tdata2/tcontrol/mcontext)
62	};
63	
64	// Map an Andes CSR (by address) to the feature gate that enables it. Addresses
65	// are the HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST scalars plus the PMA block. A CSR with no
66	// custom-extension gate is ALWAYS (a base machine CSR every Andes core has).
67	// Maintainer note: a CSR added to HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST that needs gating must
68	// get a case here, else it defaults to ALWAYS (transported unconditionally).
69	constexpr AndesGate andes_gate_for(uint16_t csr_addr)
70	{
71	  switch (csr_addr) {
72	    case 0x801: return AndesGate::DSP;           // ucode (DSP overflow flag)
73	    case 0x800: return AndesGate::CODENSE;        // uitb  (CoDense table base)
74	    // jvt is Zcmt's table-jump base, NOT part of classic CoDense (exec.it +
75	    // uitb): a CoDense core without Zcmt faults a csrr of it (seen on
76	    // ax45mpv_premium, where it aborted the drain CSR sweep).
77	    case 0x017: return AndesGate::ZCMT;           // jvt   (Zcmt only)
78	    case 0x7C5: return AndesGate::POWERBRAKE;     // mpft_ctl
79	    case 0x7C2: return AndesGate::ECC;            // mecc_code
80	    case 0x7C6:                                   // mhsp_ctl
81	    case 0x7C7:                                   // msp_bound
82	    case 0x7C8: return AndesGate::STACKSAFE;      // msp_base
83	    case 0x7C0: return AndesGate::ILM;            // milmb (ILM base)
84	    case 0x7C1: return AndesGate::DLM;            // mdlmb (DLM base)
85	    // v4 M-ext CSR gates (HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST).
86	    // The PMNDS counter block (SPA existence: mmsc_cfg.PMNDS, plus misa[20]
87	    // or misa[18] for the U/S members). Over-claiming any of these faults a
88	    // PB csrr with cmderr=3, aborting a CSR sweep -- seen live for 0x7D1 on
89	    // premium (M-only) and 0x7CF on advanced (Sscofpmf replaces PMNDS).
90	    case 0x7CF: return AndesGate::PMNDS;          // mcounterinten
91	    case 0x7CE: case 0x7D1: case 0x7D3:           // mcounterwen, mcountermask_m/_u
92	      return AndesGate::PMNDS_UMODE;
93	    case 0x7D2: return AndesGate::PMNDS_SMODE;    // mcountermask_s
94	    case 0x30A: case 0x306:                       // menvcfg, mcounteren
95	    case 0x808: case 0x80B: case 0x811:           // uzobctl, ucctlbeginaddr, sleepvalue
96	      return AndesGate::UMODE;
97	    // umisc_ctl: "Access Mode: User and above" is WHO may touch it, not an
98	    // existence condition -- spec existence is ALT_FP_FMT | CST_CTL (RTL:
99	    // BFLOAT16_ARITH | ACE, no privilege term). The UMODE gate under-claimed
100	    // it on both (M-only) engines; found by the registration audit.
101	    case 0x813: return AndesGate::ALT_FP;
102	    case 0x7D5: return AndesGate::SMODE;          // mslideleg
103	    case 0x747: return AndesGate::EPMP;           // mseccfg
104	    // The STANDARD counters exist under either perf-monitor scheme (Zihpm);
105	    // only the Andes PMNDS block above is scheme-dependent.
106	    case 0x320: case 0xB03: case 0xB04: case 0xB05: case 0xB06:  // mcountinhibit, mhpmcounter3-6
107	    case 0x323: case 0x324: case 0x325: case 0x326:              // mhpmevent3-6
108	      return AndesGate::PERF_MONITOR;
109	    case 0x740: case 0x741: case 0x742: case 0x744:  // mnscratch, mnepc, mncause, mnstatus
110	    case 0x7DE:                                       // mrnxvec
111	      return AndesGate::SMRNMI;
112	    // mnvec is base Andes NMI state -- spec "IM Requirement: Required", RTL
113	    // decodes it unconditionally on cores that lack Smrnmi entirely. It was
114	    // wrongly grouped with the Smrnmi CSRs and under-claimed on every engine.
115	    case 0x7C3:                                   // mnvec
116	    case 0x7C9: return AndesGate::ALWAYS;         // mdcause (base Andes trap CSR)
117	    case 0x7D6: case 0x7D7: case 0x7D8: case 0x7D9:  // msavestatus, msaveepc1, msavecause1, msaveepc2
118	    case 0x7DA: case 0x7DB: case 0x7DC:              // msavecause2, msavedcause1, msavedcause2
119	      return AndesGate::EXCSLVL;
120	    case 0x307: case 0x347: case 0x7EC:           // mtvt, mintthresh, mcirq_entry
121	      return AndesGate::CLIC;
122	    case 0x30C: case 0x30D: case 0x30E: case 0x30F:  // mstateen0..3
123	      return AndesGate::SMSTATEEN;
124	    case 0x7CB: case 0x7CD: return AndesGate::CCTL;  // mcctlbeginaddr, mcctldata
125	    case 0x7F0: return AndesGate::PPI;            // mppib
126	    case 0x7F1: return AndesGate::FIO;            // mfiob
127	    case 0x7A0: case 0x7A1: case 0x7A2: case 0x7A5: case 0x7A8:  // tselect, tdata1, tdata2, tcontrol, mcontext
128	      return AndesGate::TRIGGER;
129	    default:
130	      // PMA cfg (0xBC0, 0xBC2) and addr (0xBD0..0xBDF) blocks.
131	      if (csr_addr == HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR || csr_addr == HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR + 2)
132	        return AndesGate::PMA;
133	      if (csr_addr >= HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR &&
134	          csr_addr < HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR + HYBRID_PMA_ADDR_NUM)
135	        return AndesGate::PMA;
136	      return AndesGate::ALWAYS;                    // mxstatus 0x7C4, mclk_ctl 0x7DF
137	  }
138	}
139	
140	// The set of Andes feature gates a target core has on. Built from the core's
141	// compiled-in config (config.inc) in the sim binary and injected into the
142	// resume/drain loops, so they transport only the CSRs the core implements.
143	// Default = every gate on (all(): no gating, the prior unconditional behavior).
144	struct AndesCaps {
145	  uint32_t gate_mask = ~0u;
146	
147	  static constexpr AndesCaps all()  { return AndesCaps{~0u}; }
148	  static constexpr AndesCaps none() { return AndesCaps{0u}; }
149	
150	  constexpr void set(AndesGate g, bool on = true)
151	  {
152	    const uint32_t bit = 1u << static_cast<unsigned>(g);
153	    if (on) gate_mask |= bit;
154	    else    gate_mask &= ~bit;
155	  }
156	
157	  constexpr bool gate_on(AndesGate g) const
158	  {
159	    return (gate_mask >> static_cast<unsigned>(g)) & 1u;
160	  }
161	
162	  // ALWAYS-gated CSRs are present on every core regardless of the mask.
163	  constexpr bool supports_csr(uint16_t csr_addr) const
164	  {
165	    const AndesGate g = andes_gate_for(csr_addr);
166	    return g == AndesGate::ALWAYS || gate_on(g);
167	  }
168	};
169	
170	// F6: build the caps from the CSR addresses the registered manifest transports,
171	// instead of from config macros (andes_caps_from_config). The transported set is
172	// a union of COMPLETE gate-groups -- supports_csr() keys on the gate, so every
173	// CSR sharing a gate transports together -- hence setting each transported CSR's
174	// gate reconstructs the EXACT caps. This lets the runtime be driven by the
175	// measured/registered manifest, making the config->caps model (the andesim
176	// mirror + parity guard) redundant. Verilator-free, so it stays unit-testable.
177	inline AndesCaps andes_caps_from_transport_set(const std::vector<uint16_t>& transported)
178	{
179	  AndesCaps c = AndesCaps::none();
180	  for (const uint16_t addr : transported)
181	    c.set(andes_gate_for(addr), true);
182	  return c;
183	}
184	
185	// The gated CSR names this core supports, for the --describe card. Iterates the
186	// two single-source-of-truth X-macro lists: the v3 Andes custom CSRs and the v4
187	// M-ext CSRs. The driver uses this list to gate --verify, so a CSR the core
188	// lacks is neither restored, drained, nor compared.
189	inline std::vector<std::string> supported_andes_csr_names(const AndesCaps& caps)
190	{
191	  std::vector<std::string> out;
192	#define X(field, addr, name) if (caps.supports_csr(addr)) out.push_back(name);
193	  HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)
194	#undef X
195	  // PMA group markers (whole pmacfg[]/pmaaddr[] blocks share one gate), so a
196	  // consumer can include/exclude PMA without listing all 18 entries.
197	  if (caps.supports_csr(HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR))  out.push_back("pmacfg");
198	  if (caps.supports_csr(HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR)) out.push_back("pmaaddr");
199	  // v4 M-ext CSRs share the same address->gate map and --describe list.
200	#define X(field, addr, name) if (caps.supports_csr(addr)) out.push_back(name);
201	  HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST(X)
202	#undef X
203	  return out;
204	}
205	
206	}  // namespace hybrid
207	
208	#endif  // ANDES_HYBRID_ANDES_CAPS_HPP

1	// Build an AndesCaps from the core's compiled-in config.inc feature macros
2	// (_NDS_*, supplied by the build-generated cpu_config.hpp). This is the ONE
3	// place that binds each Andes feature gate to its config macro -- the sim-binary
4	// counterpart of the Verilator-free andes_caps.hpp, kept separate so the unit
5	// tests never need the generated header.
6	//
7	// PRECONDITION: the _NDS_* macros must already be in scope (include this AFTER
8	// cpu_config.hpp). A macro that is absent reads as "feature off" (gate clear),
9	// never a compile error -- so a core whose config omits a knob stays safe.
10	#pragma once
11	
12	#include "hybrid/andes_caps.hpp"
13	
14	namespace hybrid {
15	
16	inline AndesCaps andes_caps_from_config()
17	{
18	  AndesCaps c = AndesCaps::none();
19	
20	#if defined(_NDS_DSP_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_DSP_SUPPORT_INT
21	  c.set(AndesGate::DSP);           // ucode
22	#endif
23	#if defined(_NDS_CODENSE_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_CODENSE_SUPPORT_INT

25	#endif
26	  // Zcmt (jvt): the RTL gates jvt on ZCE_SUPPORT_INT (kv_csr_dec.v); newer
27	  // config.inc generations carry NDS_ZCE_SUPPORT_INT (advanced: 0), older
28	  // ones (premium) have no knob at all -- absent reads as "feature off".
29	#if (defined(_NDS_ZCMT_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_ZCMT_SUPPORT_INT) || \
30	    (defined(_NDS_ZCE_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_ZCE_SUPPORT_INT)
31	  c.set(AndesGate::ZCMT);          // jvt
32	#endif
33	#if defined(_NDS_POWERBRAKE_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_POWERBRAKE_SUPPORT_INT
34	  c.set(AndesGate::POWERBRAKE);    // mpft_ctl
35	#endif
36	#if defined(_NDS_STACKSAFE_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_STACKSAFE_SUPPORT_INT
37	  c.set(AndesGate::STACKSAFE);     // mhsp_ctl, msp_bound, msp_base
38	#endif

40	  c.set(AndesGate::PERF_MONITOR);  // mcountinhibit, mhpmcounter/event3-6
41	  // Andes PMNDS scheme (mcounterinten, mcounterwen, mcountermask_*): exists
42	  // only when the standard Sscofpmf scheme does NOT replace it (RTL:
43	  // PERFORMANCE_MONITOR_INT==1 & SSCOFPMF_SUPPORT==0), plus the privilege
44	  // term the SPA conditions carry.
45	#if !defined(_NDS_SSCOFPMF_SUPPORT) || !_NDS_SSCOFPMF_SUPPORT
46	  c.set(AndesGate::PMNDS);
47	#if defined(_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS) && (_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS >= 2)
48	  c.set(AndesGate::PMNDS_UMODE);
49	#endif
50	#if defined(_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS) && (_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS >= 3)
51	  c.set(AndesGate::PMNDS_SMODE);
52	#endif
53	#endif
54	#endif
55	#if defined(_NDS_PMA_ENTRIES) && (_NDS_PMA_ENTRIES > 0)
56	  c.set(AndesGate::PMA);           // pmacfg / pmaaddr
57	#endif
58	#if defined(_NDS_ILM_SIZE_KB) && (_NDS_ILM_SIZE_KB > 0)
59	  c.set(AndesGate::ILM);           // milmb
60	#endif
61	#if defined(_NDS_DLM_SIZE_KB) && (_NDS_DLM_SIZE_KB > 0)
62	  c.set(AndesGate::DLM);           // mdlmb
63	#endif
64	  // ECC: mecc_code exists if ANY RAM block is configured with ECC.
65	#if (defined(_NDS_DCACHE_ECC_TYPE_INT) && _NDS_DCACHE_ECC_TYPE_INT) || \
66	    (defined(_NDS_ICACHE_ECC_TYPE_INT) && _NDS_ICACHE_ECC_TYPE_INT) || \
67	    (defined(_NDS_ILM_ECC_TYPE_INT)    && _NDS_ILM_ECC_TYPE_INT)    || \
68	    (defined(_NDS_DLM_ECC_TYPE_INT)    && _NDS_DLM_ECC_TYPE_INT)
69	  c.set(AndesGate::ECC);           // mecc_code
70	#endif
71	
72	  // v4 M-ext gates. Privilege-level gates from NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS
73	  // (1 = M, 2 = M+U, 3 = M+S+U). An absent knob reads as off -- safe.
74	#if defined(_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS) && (_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS >= 2)
75	  c.set(AndesGate::UMODE);         // menvcfg, mcounteren, mcountermask_u, U-delta
76	#endif
77	#if defined(_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS) && (_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS >= 3)
78	  c.set(AndesGate::SMODE);         // mcountermask_s, mslideleg
79	#endif
80	#if defined(_NDS_NUM_TRIGGER) && (_NDS_NUM_TRIGGER > 0)
81	  c.set(AndesGate::TRIGGER);       // tselect, tdata1, tdata2, tcontrol, mcontext
82	#endif
83	#if (defined(_NDS_SMEPMP) && _NDS_SMEPMP) || (defined(_NDS_EPMP) && _NDS_EPMP)
84	  c.set(AndesGate::EPMP);          // mseccfg
85	#endif
86	#if (defined(_NDS_SMRNMI) && _NDS_SMRNMI) || (defined(_NDS_RNMI) && _NDS_RNMI)
87	  c.set(AndesGate::SMRNMI);        // mnscratch/mnepc/mncause/mnstatus/mnvec/mrnxvec
88	#endif
89	#if defined(_NDS_EXCSLVL) && (_NDS_EXCSLVL > 0)
90	  c.set(AndesGate::EXCSLVL);       // msave*
91	#endif
92	#if (defined(_NDS_ECLIC) && _NDS_ECLIC) || (defined(_NDS_CLIC) && _NDS_CLIC)
93	  c.set(AndesGate::CLIC);          // mtvt, mintthresh, mcirq_entry
94	#endif
95	#if defined(_NDS_SMSTATEEN) && _NDS_SMSTATEEN
96	  c.set(AndesGate::SMSTATEEN);     // mstateen0..3
97	#endif
98	  // CCTL: the RTL gates the mcctl* CSRs on cache presence (CACHE_SUPPORT_INT
99	  // -- the spec's mmsc_cfg.CCTLCSR follows the cache RAMs on this family);
100	  // no config generation emits a dedicated NDS_CCTLCSR knob, so bind the
101	  // cache sizes too. Found as a live under-claim on both built engines.
102	#if (defined(_NDS_CCTLCSR) && _NDS_CCTLCSR) || (defined(_NDS_CCTL) && _NDS_CCTL) || \
103	    (defined(_NDS_ICACHE_SIZE_KB) && (_NDS_ICACHE_SIZE_KB > 0)) || \
104	    (defined(_NDS_DCACHE_SIZE_KB) && (_NDS_DCACHE_SIZE_KB > 0))

106	#endif

108	#if (defined(_NDS_BFLOAT16_ARITH_SUPPORT) && _NDS_BFLOAT16_ARITH_SUPPORT) || \
109	    (defined(_NDS_ACE_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_ACE_SUPPORT_INT)
110	  c.set(AndesGate::ALT_FP);        // umisc_ctl
111	#endif
112	#if defined(_NDS_PPI_SIZE_KB) && (_NDS_PPI_SIZE_KB > 0)
113	  c.set(AndesGate::PPI);           // mppib
114	#endif
115	#if (defined(_NDS_FIO_SIZE_KB) && (_NDS_FIO_SIZE_KB > 0)) || \
116	    (defined(_NDS_FIO) && _NDS_FIO)

1	// V-register transport staging: the host<->guest-RAM half of the V data
2	// regfile transfer. The Debug Module abstract-command space has no slots for
3	// v0..v31 (the RISC-V Debug Spec leaves V to the Program Buffer or
4	// implementation-specific extensions), so vsim moves v0..v31 by executing a
5	// vle8.v/vse8.v sweep on the halted hart through the Program Buffer (see
6	// pb_v_data_sweep in program_buffer.hpp, driven by ResumeDriver on resume and
7	// StateDrain at drain). That sweep loads/stores the V scratch region of guest
8	// RAM -- the top page of the mapped span (v_scratch_gpa, L26); this header
9	// provides the matching host-side copy:
10	//
11	//   - stage_v_to_scratch: state.vreg[] -> scratch RAM, called before resume so
12	//     the ResumeDriver vle8.v sweep reads QEMU 1's V values.
13	//   - read_v_from_scratch: scratch RAM -> state.vreg[], called after the
14	//     StateDrain vse8.v sweep so the drained v0..v31 land in state.vreg[]
15	//     (the handoff file).
16	//
17	// The transfer is transparent to the workload: benchmark binaries issue no
18	// transport code, only the enter_vsim / exit_vsim markers. rt_c_v_regs.c is
19	// the reference fixture.
20	//
21	// Pure logic: no SystemC, no DMI bus. Easy to unit-test.
22	
23	#pragma once
24	
25	#include "hybrid/andes_caps.hpp"
26	#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
27	
28	#include <cstddef>
29	#include <cstdint>
30	#include <cstring>
31	#include <span>
32	#include <stdexcept>
33	
34	namespace hybrid
35	{
36	
37	// Total scratch bytes needed: 32 V regs × HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX. Sized to the
38	// maximum supported VLEN; the actual per-reg byte count is `vlenb`. Defined in
39	// the shared ABI (HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES) so the driver's mmap sizing and this
40	// consumer agree on one count (L26/F2).
41	inline constexpr std::size_t kVScratchBytes = HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES;
42	
43	// L26: the scratch region is the TOP kVScratchBytes of the mapped RAM span,
44	// not a fixed address. Scheme D parks it just above the program's declared
45	// RAM (the driver maps one page more than --mem-size), so no program layout
46	// can collide with it. This is the single source of truth for the GUEST
47	// address the Program-Buffer sweep (ResumeDriver/StateDrain) loads/stores
48	// through; the host stager below copies span-relative and needs no base.
49	inline constexpr auto v_scratch_gpa(uint64_t ram_base, std::size_t ram_size)
50	  -> uint64_t
51	{
52	  return ram_base + static_cast<uint64_t>(ram_size) - kVScratchBytes;
53	}
54	
55	// Sentinel for "no V scratch configured". ResumeDriver/StateDrain default to
56	// it; a non-V handoff never consults the scratch GPA, so that is fine, but if
57	// a V handoff reaches the sweep with the GPA still unset the driver throws
58	// (loud) rather than silently transporting V through a bogus address.
59	inline constexpr uint64_t kVScratchGpaUnset =
60	  static_cast<uint64_t>(-1);
61	
62	// GPR block-load prototype: x1..x31 (8 bytes each) staged in the TOP of the
63	// scratch page so the resume ld-sweep reads them below the V region (which
64	// grows up from the base). Reusing the V page keeps this single-repo; it only
65	// applies when the V data leaves room (gpr_scratch_fits), else the caller falls
66	// back to per-register abstract writes. A production version would give the GPR
67	// block its own scratch page instead of sharing the V one.
68	inline constexpr std::size_t kGprScratchBytes = 31 * 8;  // x1..x31
69	
70	inline constexpr auto gpr_scratch_gpa(uint64_t v_scratch_base) -> uint64_t
71	{
72	  return v_scratch_base + kVScratchBytes - kGprScratchBytes;
73	}
74	
75	inline constexpr auto gpr_scratch_fits(uint64_t vlenb) -> bool
76	{
77	  return static_cast<std::size_t>(32) * vlenb <= kVScratchBytes - kGprScratchBytes;
78	}
79	
80	// FPR block-load: f0..f31 (8 bytes each) staged just BELOW the GPR block. Unlike
81	// x0, f0 is a real register, so all 32 f-regs ride the sweep (kFprScratchBytes =
82	// 32*8, not 31*8). The two blocks are disjoint and staged up front, so the FPR
83	// fld-sweep (early in resume) and the GPR ld-sweep (later) never collide. The V
84	// region grows up from the base, so the fit gate here is tighter than the GPR
85	// one -- V must clear both blocks.
86	inline constexpr std::size_t kFprScratchBytes = 32 * 8;  // f0..f31
87	
88	inline constexpr auto fpr_scratch_gpa(uint64_t v_scratch_base) -> uint64_t
89	{
90	  return v_scratch_base + kVScratchBytes - kGprScratchBytes - kFprScratchBytes;
91	}
92	
93	inline constexpr auto fpr_scratch_fits(uint64_t vlenb) -> bool
94	{
95	  return static_cast<std::size_t>(32) * vlenb
96	         <= kVScratchBytes - kGprScratchBytes - kFprScratchBytes;
97	}
98	
99	// CSR block (v3/v4): the Andes V5 + M-ext CSRs the sweep transports through the
100	// Program Buffer ride a scratch region just BELOW the FPR block. Sized to hold
101	// the MAX possible set (every defined CSR); the live count is smaller (flag- and
102	// caps-gated) and packs contiguously from slot 0. Slots = 13 Andes scalars + PMA
103	// (2 pmacfg + 16 pmaaddr) + 51 M-ext, auto-counted from the shared X-macros so
104	// the size never drifts as CSRs are added.
105	inline constexpr std::size_t kCsrScratchSlots = [] {
106	  std::size_t n = 0;
107	#define X(field, addr, name) ++n;
108	  HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)
109	  HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST(X)
110	#undef X
111	  return n + HYBRID_PMA_CFG_NUM + HYBRID_PMA_ADDR_NUM;
112	}();
113	inline constexpr std::size_t kCsrScratchBytes = kCsrScratchSlots * 8;
114	
115	inline constexpr auto csr_scratch_gpa(uint64_t v_scratch_base) -> uint64_t
116	{
117	  return v_scratch_base + kVScratchBytes - kGprScratchBytes - kFprScratchBytes
118	         - kCsrScratchBytes;
119	}
120	
121	inline constexpr auto csr_scratch_fits(uint64_t vlenb) -> bool
122	{
123	  return static_cast<std::size_t>(32) * vlenb
124	         <= kVScratchBytes - kGprScratchBytes - kFprScratchBytes
125	              - kCsrScratchBytes;
126	}
127	
128	namespace detail
129	{
130	
131	// Byte offset of the scratch region inside a RAM span: its top page. Throws
132	// if the span is smaller than one scratch page (a too-small RAM mapping).
133	inline auto scratch_offset(std::size_t ram_size) -> std::size_t
134	{
135	  if (ram_size < kVScratchBytes)
136	    throw std::runtime_error(
137	      "v_regfile_xfer: RAM span smaller than the V scratch page");
138	  return ram_size - kVScratchBytes;
139	}
140	
141	}  // namespace detail
142	
143	// Walk every CSR the sweep transports, in canonical order -- Andes scalars, PMA
144	// ADDR, PMA CFG, then M-ext -- gated by the live block flag AND engine caps.
145	// Invokes fn(slot_index, csr_addr, field_ref) per transported CSR: the host
146	// stage copies field->scratch, the host lift copies scratch->field, and the
147	// ResumeDriver/StateDrain build their PB sweep's addr list -- all walking THIS
148	// identical order, so scratch slot i and csrs[i] always agree. State is
149	// templated so it binds const (stage / restore) and mutable (lift). PMA addr
150	// precedes cfg because the restore's TOR/NAPOT cfg consumes the addr already in
151	// place (mirrors the PMP/PMA restore ordering). Applies the same `(flags & FLAG)
152	// && caps.supports_csr(addr)` predicate every consumer of the block uses, so the
153	// single X-macro keeps them in lockstep.
154	template<typename State, typename Fn>
155	inline void for_each_sweep_csr(State& state, const AndesCaps& caps, Fn&& fn)
156	{
157	  std::size_t i = 0;
158	  if (state.flags & HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES) {
159	#define X(field, addr, name) \
160	  if (caps.supports_csr(addr)) { fn(i, uint16_t(addr), state.andes.field); ++i; }
161	    HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)
162	#undef X
163	    for (int p = 0; p < HYBRID_PMA_ADDR_NUM; ++p)
164	      if (caps.supports_csr(HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR + p)) {
165	        fn(i, uint16_t(HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR + p), state.andes.pmaaddr[p]); ++i;
166	      }
167	    for (int p = 0; p < HYBRID_PMA_CFG_NUM; ++p)
168	      if (caps.supports_csr(HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR + 2 * p)) {
169	        fn(i, uint16_t(HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR + 2 * p), state.andes.pmacfg[p]); ++i;
170	      }
171	  }
172	  if (state.flags & HYBRID_FLAG_M_EXT) {
173	#define X(field, addr, name) \
174	  if (caps.supports_csr(addr)) { fn(i, uint16_t(addr), state.m_ext.field); ++i; }
175	    HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST(X)
176	#undef X
177	  }
178	}

180	// Copy state.vreg[] into the span's top scratch page. Called just before vsim
181	// resumes the hart so the fixture can vle8.v from scratch and pick up QEMU 1's
182	// V values.
183	inline void stage_v_to_scratch(const hybrid_state_v1& state,
184	                               std::span<uint8_t> ram)
185	{
186	  const auto off = detail::scratch_offset(ram.size());
187	  // Pack at vlenb stride (drop the wire-format padding) so v0..v31 sit
188	  // contiguously and the Program-Buffer sweep can move 8 at a time via LMUL=8.
189	  const std::size_t vlenb = state.vlenb;
190	  for (std::size_t r = 0; r < 32; ++r)
191	    std::memcpy(ram.data() + off + r * vlenb,
192	                state.vreg + r * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX, vlenb);
193	}
194	
195	// Pack x1..x31 (8 bytes each) contiguously into the top kGprScratchBytes of the
196	// scratch page; the resume ld-sweep reads them back. state.gpr[1..31] is itself
197	// contiguous, so this is a single memcpy. Called before resume, gated by the
198	// caller on gpr_scratch_fits (the V region must leave room in the page).
199	inline void stage_gpr_to_scratch(const hybrid_state_v1& state,
200	                                 std::span<uint8_t> ram)
201	{
202	  const auto off =
203	    detail::scratch_offset(ram.size()) + (kVScratchBytes - kGprScratchBytes);
204	  std::memcpy(ram.data() + off, &state.gpr[1], 31 * 8);
205	}
206	
207	// Pack f0..f31 (8 bytes each) contiguously into the scratch page just below the
208	// GPR block; the resume fld-sweep reads them back. state.fpr[0..31] is itself
209	// contiguous, so this is a single memcpy. Called before resume, gated by the
210	// caller on fpr_scratch_fits (the V region must leave room for both blocks).
211	inline void stage_fpr_to_scratch(const hybrid_state_v1& state,
212	                                 std::span<uint8_t> ram)
213	{
214	  const auto off = detail::scratch_offset(ram.size())
215	                   + (kVScratchBytes - kGprScratchBytes - kFprScratchBytes);
216	  std::memcpy(ram.data() + off, &state.fpr[0], 32 * 8);
217	}
218	
219	// Copy the span's top scratch page into state.vreg[]. Called inside the vsim
220	// drain path after the fixture's prologue vse8.v has settled the (possibly
221	// mutated) regfile bytes into RAM.
222	inline void read_v_from_scratch(hybrid_state_v1& state,
223	                                std::span<const uint8_t> ram)
224	{
225	  const auto off = detail::scratch_offset(ram.size());
226	  // Unpack the vlenb-packed scratch back into the wire-strided vreg[] slots.
227	  // Each slot's padding (bytes vlenb..HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX) is left as-is:
228	  // callers pass a passthrough state whose padding is already zero (the QEMU
229	  // drain zero-fills it), so the full 128-byte slots stay byte-identical to the
230	  // oracle that --verify compares against.
231	  const std::size_t vlenb = state.vlenb;
232	  for (std::size_t r = 0; r < 32; ++r)
233	    std::memcpy(state.vreg + r * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX,
234	                ram.data() + off + r * vlenb, vlenb);
235	}
236	
237	// Lift `count` GPRs (x1..x[count]) out of the scratch page into state.gpr[].
238	// Mirror of stage_gpr_to_scratch, reading from the identical top-of-page offset:
239	// the drain sd-sweep stored them here from the regfile. count is < 31 when the
240	// sweep's base register (itself a GPR) was captured separately via an abstract
241	// read and excluded from the sweep, so its slot must not be lifted.
242	inline void read_gpr_from_scratch(hybrid_state_v1& state,
243	                                  std::span<const uint8_t> ram,
244	                                  std::size_t count)
245	{
246	  const auto off =
247	    detail::scratch_offset(ram.size()) + (kVScratchBytes - kGprScratchBytes);
248	  std::memcpy(&state.gpr[1], ram.data() + off, count * 8);
249	}
250	
251	// Lift f0..f31 out of the scratch page into state.fpr[]. Mirror of
252	// stage_fpr_to_scratch; the drain fsd-sweep stored them here. No f-reg is the
253	// sweep's base (that is an integer GPR), so all 32 round-trip.
254	inline void read_fpr_from_scratch(hybrid_state_v1& state,
255	                                  std::span<const uint8_t> ram)
256	{
257	  const auto off = detail::scratch_offset(ram.size())
258	                   + (kVScratchBytes - kGprScratchBytes - kFprScratchBytes);
259	  std::memcpy(&state.fpr[0], ram.data() + off, 32 * 8);
260	}
261	
262	// Pack the transported Andes+M-ext CSR values into the CSR scratch region (just
263	// below the FPR block) in canonical order; the resume csr_sweep ld's them into
264	// each CSR. Called before resume, gated per-CSR on flag + caps (for_each_sweep_
265	// csr), so an engine's unsupported CSRs never take a slot.
266	inline void stage_csr_to_scratch(const hybrid_state_v1& state,
267	                                 std::span<uint8_t> ram, const AndesCaps& caps)
268	{
269	  const auto base =
270	    detail::scratch_offset(ram.size())
271	    + (kVScratchBytes - kGprScratchBytes - kFprScratchBytes - kCsrScratchBytes);
272	  for_each_sweep_csr(state, caps,
273	    [&](std::size_t i, uint16_t /*addr*/, const uint64_t& value) {
274	      std::memcpy(ram.data() + base + i * 8, &value, 8);
275	    });
276	}
277	
278	// Lift the Andes+M-ext CSR values out of the CSR scratch region into state, the
279	// mirror of stage_csr_to_scratch: the drain csr_sweep sd'd them here. Same
280	// flag+caps-gated canonical order, so slot i lands in the field it came from.
281	inline void read_csr_from_scratch(hybrid_state_v1& state,
282	                                  std::span<const uint8_t> ram,
283	                                  const AndesCaps& caps)
284	{
285	  const auto base =
286	    detail::scratch_offset(ram.size())
287	    + (kVScratchBytes - kGprScratchBytes - kFprScratchBytes - kCsrScratchBytes);
288	  for_each_sweep_csr(state, caps,
289	    [&](std::size_t i, uint16_t /*addr*/, uint64_t& value) {
290	      std::memcpy(&value, ram.data() + base + i * 8, 8);
291	    });
292	}
